nodes.label: Admins delay inviting the team because plan/seat/permission decisions are not surfaced first

provenance.quote: I didn't want to start a workspace and then have to redo it once everyone was in. So I needed admin stuff first — who can invite, what permissions, that kind of thing.
Admins are blocked early on plan/seat decisions and never invite the team, so the trial never gets used.

nodes.label: Invite-flow upgrade popup is misread as a mid-trial paywall

provenance.quote: I'm trying to invite my 8 teammates and after the third one I got a popup saying I have to upgrade to Team plan. The trial said unlimited seats — what is going on?
The wording said "upgrade to continue." It should say "after your trial, this plan starts at X."

nodes.label: Admins discover the budgeted plan's seat limit is lower than headcount only after starting the invite flow

provenance.quote: we had budget approval for one tier and the invite limit on it was lower than our headcount. So I had to go back to finance, which is another two days.

nodes.label: CSV imports drop comment history, forcing teams to keep the old tool alive as a read-only archive

provenance.quote: The CSV import worked but lost all the comment history. We ended up keeping Trello open for a month as the read-only archive.
Issues came over, but every comment thread on every issue is gone. We have 18 months of context in those comments and we can't lose it.

nodes.label: Jira's CSV export fields don't align with Pebble's import schema, so users abandon the import attempt

provenance.quote: The Jira CSV export is a mess — fields don't line up. I spent maybe an hour fighting with the import and then gave up.

nodes.label: Trial sample workspace doesn't help users judge whether the tool fits *their* actual work

provenance.quote: The sample project is cute but it's not my work. I can't tell if a tool fits my actual situation by clicking around a demo workspace.

nodes.label: Permissions flow for scoping contractors to specific projects is buried two settings menus deep

provenance.quote: I wanted them in specific projects only, not the whole workspace, and that flow is buried two settings menus deep. I figured it out, but I had to figure it out.

nodes.label: Team rollouts stall when import does not preserve historical data fidelity

provenance.quote: We're stalled on the rollout until this works.

nodes.label: Linear — referenced as the model for admin-first onboarding sequencing

nodes.label: For ops-led mid-market admins, SSO working first try is the single biggest signal of "will this be ops-painful or not."

provenance.quote: your SSO with Okta worked first try. That's the single biggest piece of "is this going to be ops-painful or not."

nodes.label: Adoption spreads inside a team when one person builds a visibly-good artifact (e.g. a useful board) — "the product adopted itself"

provenance.quote: someone built a really nice bug board in Pebble and word spread and now everyone's in there. The product adopted itself the moment one person showed what good looked like in it.

nodes.label: Sequencing admin decisions before product surface is a forcing function for procrastinated decisions, not just a setup wizard

provenance.quote: The four-question gate forces the admin to make exactly the decisions they were going to have to make anyway, in the order the product is about to need them.

nodes.label: A seasoned mid-market ops-led admin prefers SSO + docs + being left alone over a guided walkthrough

provenance.quote: A native Okta-provisioning flow would have saved me an hour. Other than that I'm a happy admin.

nodes.label: Native-Jira-import-with-comments has been a recurring support request (at least six this month per internal note)

provenance.quote: This is the 6th request for native-Jira-with-comments this month.

nodes.label: Trial-to-paid conversion in SMB and mid-market cohorts (28% Q4 → 19% Q1; Q2 goal is to recover the gap)

provenance.quote: Trial-to-paid conversion fell from 28% to 19% across Q4 → Q1 in the SMB and mid-market cohorts. Q2 priority is to recover the gap, not to push new top-of-funnel acquisition.

nodes.label: 41% of trial workspaces never reach 3 active seats

provenance.quote: 41% of trial workspaces never reach 3 active seats.

nodes.label: Workspaces hitting 2+ projects with real activity by day 7 convert at >50%; 0–1 convert at <10%

provenance.quote: Workspaces that hit 2+ projects with real activity by day 7 convert at >50%. Workspaces with 0–1 convert at <10%.

nodes.label: Trials whose admin uses our Jira or Asana import convert at 38% vs. 14% for trials that don't import

provenance.quote: Trials where the admin uses our Jira or Asana import convert at 38% vs. 14% for trials that don't import.

nodes.label: The proposed pre-setup admin walkthrough solves the "I'll come back later" problem rather than merely delaying it earlier in the flow
nodes.risk: If wrong, the walkthrough is a longer abandoned step rather than a forcing function — and we ship a quarter of scope that doesn't move trial→paid conversion.

nodes.label: Mid-market admins actually want a guided pre-setup walkthrough rather than docs + SSO and otherwise being left alone
nodes.risk: If wrong, we build a flow the most valuable cohort (mid-market) actively avoids; Sam at GreenCo is single-source evidence pointing the opposite direction.

nodes.label: Import friction is the *cause* of trial churn, not just the visible trigger for users already leaning out
nodes.risk: If wrong, GA-ing the native Jira import alone moves conversion less than expected — and we miss the underlying cause (e.g. admin paralysis pre-invite) that the import was masking.
